related_questions.question: How does a reverse mortgage work in California?
related_questions.snippet: With a reverse mortgage, the bank pays you from the equity in your home. There is no restriction on how you can use the money. The bank gets repaid when you sell your home, refinance, permanently move out, or pass away. At that time, you or your heirs must repay the loan plus interest in one payment.

related_questions.question: What is the biggest problem with a reverse mortgage?
related_questions.snippet: A reverse mortgage increases your debt and can use up your equity. While the amount is based on your equity, you're still borrowing the money and paying the lender a fee and interest. Your debt keeps going up (and your equity keeps going down) because interest is added to your balance every month.

related_questions.question: What is the 95% rule on a reverse mortgage?
related_questions.snippet: As an heir, you do not have to pay off the reverse mortgage balance in full to keep the property. You can keep the home for 95% of the property's market value, if that amount is lower than the loan balance. If you do not have the money to pay the balance or 95% of the market value, you still have options.
